acceptance_evidence: CCA verdict and MergeGate evidence are recorded before completion.
completion_conditions: A BEHIND branch whose repairable check is red is synced rather than repaired, bounded by MAX_BASE_SYNCS, and the sync consumes no repair attempt.
A CCA verdict of needs_guardian or blocked still produces its terminal stop, BEHIND or not.
No sync ever fires while the MergeGate policy check is red.
After MAX_BASE_SYNCS the loop behaves exactly as today, including reaching stop_guardian at the repair limit.
A repair dispatched after a sync can still deliver its push.
The closeout decision table is unchanged.
The full suite, the goal-loop suite, the adversarial-state suite and validate_shiki stay green.

decisions: MEASURED. PR #288's 'MergeGate metadata check' failed with exactly one reason: 'PR must not delete base ledger file .shiki/ledger/L-20260805T052931749888Z-3017e935.json; state_class=append-only-evidence'. That file reached main via PR #287 after the task branch forked; mergeStateStatus was BEHIND. Cycles 3/5/7 dispatched repairs, cycle 9 emitted stop_guardian. The CCA independently returned verdict=blocked naming the same cause and quoting all three repair packets.

ROOT CAUSE, read from source. `_merge_or_sync` (`scripts/shiki_loop.py:101`) is the ONLY site that emits `sync_branch`, and its own docstring says it is 'Reached only once a PR is otherwise ready to merge — every required check green'. The repairable-failure block (`:279-316`) returns `dispatch_repair` and is evaluated first. So when being BEHIND is the CAUSE of a red check, the sync path is unreachable.

THIS WAS DELIBERATE, NOT AN OVERSIGHT. `tests/test_branch_behind_sync.py:124` pins it: `test_behind_but_failing_check_is_not_synced`, commented 'Not otherwise ready: a failing check repairs, never syncs.' The task is therefore to NARROW that exclusion under stated conditions, not to reorder the decision function. The test inverts and must say why.

REJECTED FIRST DESIGN — placement. 'Return sync_branch instead of dispatch_repair when BEHIND' placed at the top of the `if repairable_failed:` block PREEMPTS the CCA verdict terminal stops at `:298-302` (`_cca_verdict_stop` maps needs_guardian -> stop_guardian, blocked -> stop_blocked), laundering a Guardian stop into a head-moving sync. The measured incident's own verdict was `blocked`. The guard MUST be evaluated strictly after `_cca_verdict_stop` has returned None.

REJECTED FIRST DESIGN — termination. Verified by reading `_sync_branch` (`:1429-1525`): it appends NO ledger and compares NO heads — `git merge origin/<base>` and `git push origin HEAD:<branch>` both return 0 for a no-op. The proposed 'a sync that does not advance the head is not forward progress' bound is therefore not implementable from existing state, and would not bound a sync that legitimately advances every time the base moves. Every other repeatable remediation in this loop is bounded by state that survives the process: `repair_attempts_for` (`:552`) counts `.shiki/repairs/RP-*.json` on disk, and `cca_rerun_count` is a task-file field gated by `MAX_CCA_RERUNS` (`:57`).

BOUND, CORRECTED. Use the established pattern: a durable task-file counter (`base_sync_attempts`) gated by a new `MAX_BASE_SYNCS` constant, exactly as `cca_rerun_count`/`MAX_CCA_RERUNS` already work. VERIFIED SAFE FOR LOCKS: `.shiki/schemas/task.schema.json` has `additionalProperties: true` and does not declare `cca_rerun_count` either (18 properties), so a new task-file field needs NO schema change — which also keeps this task's locks disjoint from D-4, which owns that schema.

ESCALATION MUST SURVIVE. Once `base_sync_attempts` reaches `MAX_BASE_SYNCS`, behaviour reverts to today's exactly: dispatch_repair -> repair limit -> stop_guardian. The escalation that surfaced PR #288 to the operator at cycle 9 must remain reachable; a change that makes `if repair_attempts >= repair_limit` (`:304`) dead code for a spinning task is worse than the defect it fixes.

GOVERNANCE, CORRECTED. The first draft preserved only the 'ONLY the policy gate is red' case — which is precisely the case where NO approval exists. The damaging case is the opposite: the Guardian has posted a head-bound approval for head H while another check is red. `repairable_failed` excludes POLICY_GATE (`:275`), so `{policy: fail, CCA: fail}` + BEHIND would have fired a sync and destroyed that approval. CORRECTED RULE: never sync while POLICY_GATE is in `failed` at all. PR #288's policy check was SKIPPED, not failed, so the measured incident is still fixed.

That one rule also closes a second hole the sweep found. `evaluate_contract_approval` condition 2 compares the base snapshot to the head task directly (`scripts/shiki_contract_approval.py:193-198`) over the seven frozen governance fields. A base sync adopts base's task file wholesale, so it could RESTORE an ADR 0015 carry that base movement had defeated — turning a stop into an autonomous merge under a contract the implementation was never re-dispatched against. That state manifests as a red policy gate, which the corrected rule refuses to sync through.

NEW INTERACTION THE CURRENT SYNC PATH CANNOT REACH. `_sync_branch` works in a THROWAWAY detached checkout (`git worktree add --detach ... origin/<branch>`, `:1471`) and pushes `HEAD:<branch>`; it never updates the REGISTERED task worktree's local branch ref, and `ensure_physical_worktree` reuses an existing path without reconciling it (`scripts/shiki_runtime.py:414`). Today that is harmless because a sync is only ever followed by a merge. This change makes a sync be followed by a REPAIR, whose push (`shiki_loop.py:836`) is then a non-fast-forward, failing with a message that misdescribes the cause. Both the sync and the push live in `shiki_loop.py`, so this is fixable IN-FILE and `scripts/shiki_runtime.py` stays out of the locks — but `tests/test_loop_branch_plumbing.py` imports `_commit_and_push_implementation` directly and is therefore MUST-CHANGE, not MUST-NOT-BREAK.

LOCK-SUFFICIENCY CHECK (2026-08-05, corrected by the sweep). MUST-CHANGE: `scripts/shiki_loop.py`; `tests/test_branch_behind_sync.py` (owns the property, and `:124` inverts); `scripts/test_shiki_goal_loop.sh` — VERIFIED at `:408-417`, it counts `RP-*.json` before and after and asserts equality under the comment 'the Guardian gate never consumes a repair attempt'. That is the twin of this change's second promise and the ONLY executable surface that can prove it; `tests/test_branch_behind_sync.py` is a pure-fixture module (`:52` calls `decide_task_action` directly) and cannot observe repair packets at all. `tests/test_loop_branch_plumbing.py` — imports the push internals directly. The first draft classified the shell suite as MUST-NOT-BREAK; that was wrong and is the same lock-sufficiency error this session has made three times.

MUST-NOT-BREAK (verification command, not locks), measured: `tests/test_loop_engine.py`, `tests/test_loop_verdict_gating.py`, `tests/test_closeout.py`, `tests/test_lock_conflict_stop.py`, `tests/test_session_lease.py`, `tests/test_repair_delivery.py` — NONE of them sets `merge_state_status`, so the new branch cannot fire for them; `scripts/test_shiki_adversarial_state.sh`; and `tests/test_paired_invariants.py`, which regex-scans this exact file's SOURCE at `:546-548` for `"verdict": "..."` literals, so the implementation must not introduce one.

LEDGER TYPE: reuse an EXISTING ledger type for the sync record. Registering a NEW type requires `.shiki/schemas/ledger.schema.json` AND `scripts/validate_shiki.py:1892`'s set-equality binder to agree, which would pull both into the locks — the measured landmine that blocked an earlier task.

CLOSEOUT PATH IS OUT OF SCOPE. The closeout arm shares `_merge_or_sync` (`:260`) but its failing-check arm returns `stop_blocked`, not `dispatch_repair`, and `docs/adr/0012` pins that decision table verbatim. This change lives in the implementation-PR repairable-failure block only; the closeout decision table must be provably unchanged so the ADR stays truthful and no ADR enters the locks.

Risk is high: this changes what an autonomous loop does with a red check, next to the Guardian gate. The failure directions that matter are (a) never launder a Guardian stop or destroy a head-bound approval, and (b) never trade a terminating stop for a livelock. Both are addressed by explicit rules above and must be proved by tests, not by inspection.
grill_with_docs.source: Reproduced live on PR #288 (2026-08-05); root cause read from source; the first draft of this contract was then swept by three independent adversarial lenses (lock sufficiency, design/termination, governance regression) which invalidated its core design. The decisions below are the corrected design, and every claim carried over was re-verified by hand.

non_goals: Reordering the decision function, or changing _merge_or_sync's existing all-green behaviour.
Changing the closeout PR decision table — docs/adr/0012 pins it verbatim.
Syncing while the MergeGate policy check is red, for any reason.
Making the repair-attempt limit or its stop_guardian escalation unreachable.
Touching any file outside the declared locks.
outcome: When a PR's required check is red *because* its branch fell behind the base, the loop syncs the base in — bounded, recorded, and without consuming a repair attempt — instead of dispatching implementer repairs that are structurally incapable of fixing it. Measured 2026-08-05 on PR #288: three repairs were dispatched, each correctly diagnosed 'loop-owned base sync, not implementer-fixable' and changed nothing, the attempt limit was exhausted, and the loop emitted stop_guardian. One `git merge origin/main` made every check green and the PR merged with no further change.
title: Sync a BEHIND branch before spending repair attempts that cannot fix it
